talkTrack: One buyer this month raised a pay-as-you-go mystery-shop vendor as a reason to push back on our standard contract terms — the pitch being that they can rewrite the shop questionnaire any time, with no multi-year commitment. That flexibility is also the catch: if the criteria can change the week after a bad score, the score isn't measuring anything you can compare over time. Ask the operations leader this: when you pull up this quarter's shop results next to last year's, are you actually looking at the same test?
coverageGaps: This edition is the team's October 12 weekly digest in #industry-competitive_intel (137 items reviewed), as approved and posted there. Items from internal Gong analysis and field reports have no public link, so their source link points to the channel. Only the RealPage court item was re-checked against its primary source (the California Attorney General's release).
doNotMisdate: RealPage court ruling: the California Attorney General's release is dated October 2, 2026 and describes a ruling in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina; the release does not state the ruling date. Earlier editions dated this ruling October 4 and described it as landing two days after the New York injunction. Neither claim is supported, so cite the release date and do not say 'two days apart.'

RealPage pausing EliseAI integrations is an internal field report (customer notice on October 7), not a public announcement. Existing sites are reported as unaffected. Do not repeat it to a customer as confirmed fact.
Yardi Aspire and Cirrus counts come from Gong competitive-mention analysis of open deals this month. They count deals where the name came up, not market share or win-loss.

items.headline: A pay-as-you-go mystery-shop vendor just became a live objection — Cirrus
items.summary: A buyer cited Cirrus, an ad hoc, pay-as-you-go mystery-shopping vendor that lets them revise their questionnaire any time with no commitment, naming it as a reason to hesitate on our standard contract terms.
items.soWhat: Named in 1 open deal this month — a commitment-free, revisable scorecard cuts against the consistency a buyer needs to compare performance over time, and this is a new name for the database.

items.headline: Yardi Aspire named in 3 open deals this month — with no news to go with it
items.summary: Buyers in three active deals cite Yardi Aspire's LMS as lacking virtual training capabilities and employee-development content, though contract terms running into 2027 are keeping two of them on a dual-system timeline rather than an immediate switch.
items.soWhat: Named in 3 open deals this month with no public news from Yardi — that's itself the finding; ask what Aspire doesn't cover today and when the contract renews.

items.headline: Court keeps RealPage's rent-pricing antitrust case alive, denies motion to dismiss
items.source: California Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
items.summary: A federal court denied RealPage's bid to dismiss the multistate antitrust suit over its rent-pricing algorithm, along with exit attempts by several co-defendant landlords. Two other defendants (LivCor and Greystar) have already settled separately; claims continue against RealPage, Camden, Pinnacle, and Willow Bridge. The release is dated October 2, 2026 and does not give the ruling date.
items.soWhat: RealPage's pricing business carries unresolved legal exposure into next year — a fact worth having on hand if algorithmic pricing comes up.

items.headline: RealPage has paused new EliseAI integrations
items.summary: RealPage told customers on October 7 that it is pausing future EliseAI site activations over a product dispute. Existing sites are unaffected. This is a field report from the team's weekly digest, not a public announcement.
items.soWhat: Useful context before a renewal or expansion conversation assumes a RealPage/EliseAI pairing still works out of the box.

items.headline: Self-built training is still the most common incumbent
items.summary: Excel trackers, a homegrown "university" program, and one person running all training alone showed up in 3 of 37 open deals this month — the same count as the top named vendor. None could show who completed what training, or when.
items.soWhat: The status quo is as common in live deals as the top named vendor. Ask how they would show who completed what training, and when.
